subject.title: [Feature]: Granular session visibility — split tools.sessions.visibility into per-capability knobs

question: Should OpenClaw add a per-capability `tools.sessions.visibility` object, or should cross-agent send/read/list separation be handled through the related A2A allowlist, allowlist visibility, and per-agent visibility proposals instead?
rationale: This changes the transcript privacy boundary and public config shape, and active related proposals overlap the same session authorization surface without one settled model.

options.title: Approve unified capability object
options.body: Adopt a backward-compatible object form for send/history/list/metadata after reconciling it with allowlist, per-agent, sandbox, and A2A semantics.

options.title: Use adjacent policy scopes
options.body: Make the open A2A, allowlist, or per-agent proposals canonical if maintainers decide those satisfy the send-without-read privacy goal better than per-capability flags.

options.title: Defer until related PRs settle
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design question while active adjacent PRs are reviewed or closed.

recommendation.title: Approve unified capability object
recommendation.body: Adopt a backward-compatible object form for send/history/list/metadata after reconciling it with allowlist, per-agent, sandbox, and A2A semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal points to this handle for the shared session-tool authorization/config boundary and related product/security decisions.
